preconditions.text: At the time notifyRewardAmount() is called, IVoter(voter).totalWeight() returns zero, which can legitimately occur during early protocol operation or when voting weights temporarily drop to zero.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: When `notifyRewardAmount()` is called while `IVoter(voter).totalWeight()` returns zero, the function transfers base tokens from the minter into GaugeManager but fails to update the global index properly. The emission accounting logic computes a ratio of zero when totalWeight is zero, resulting in no index increment. Since gauge distributions rely entirely on index deltas to calculate claimable amounts, these transferred tokens become permanently inaccessible.

The vulnerable flow occurs in the notification process where totalWeight can legitimately be zero during early protocol operation or when voting weights temporarily drop to zero. The contract transfers the emission tokens but creates no mechanism to track or redistribute them once voting weight is restored. The `_updateForAfterDistribution()` function only processes index deltas, so previously unaccounted emissions remain stranded indefinitely.

The vulnerability has medium likelihood as zero-weight epochs are realistic scenarios, particularly at protocol genesis before any votes are cast or during operational periods when voting weight temporarily drops to zero. Since emission notification occurs as part of regular epoch rollover without requiring special privileges, this condition can arise under normal operation sequencing, especially during protocol launch phases.

safety.text: Emissions notified to GaugeManager must eventually be allocated to gauges and reach their intended recipients, including when notification occurs while totalWeight is zero.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: This vulnerability causes permanent loss of scheduled emissions intended for distribution to users. When totalWeight is zero during emission notification, the transferred tokens remain in GaugeManager indefinitely with no recovery mechanism. This breaks the emission distribution policy and creates unclaimable funds, undermining the protocol's token economics and causing direct financial losses to stakeholders expecting those emissions.

Consider implementing a pending emission mechanism to handle notifications when totalWeight is zero. One approach could be to track unallocated emissions in a separate variable when totalWeight is zero, then incorporate these pending amounts into the index calculation once totalWeight becomes positive. This would ensure that all notified emissions eventually reach their intended recipients regardless of timing.
